item.title: Vucic resigns as president of Serbia
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic speaks during a press conference in Belgrade, Serbia, Sept. 27, 2026. Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. (Photo by Predrag Milosavljevic/Xinhua)
BELGRADE, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president.
"I am now signing the text that reads as follows: 'Pursuant to Article 116, paragraph 5 of the Constitution of the Republic of Serbia, I submit my resignation from the office of President of the Republic.'...Ana, this goes to the Parliament, and tomorrow you go to the handover," said Vucic.
Under Serbia's Constitution and Law on the president, the president's term ends when the written resignation is formally received by the National Assembly, without requiring approval. The Speaker of the National Assembly Ana Brnabic then assumes presidential duties for up to three months and must call a presidential election within that period.
Vucic also said he would take part in the snap parliamentary elections scheduled on Oct. 25 as an ordinary citizen.
The Serbian parliament was dissolved on Sept. 9. Under the Constitution, a dissolved parliament has limited powers, while the government continues to perform its duties until a new government is formed.
On Sept. 5, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) nominated Vucic as head of its electoral list and its candidate for prime minister in the upcoming snap parliamentary elections.
Following the Oct. 25 elections, the process of forming a new government will begin. The acting president, after consulting representatives of the elected electoral lists, proposes a prime minister candidate to the National Assembly. The candidate then presents the government's program and cabinet members, which must be approved by a majority of all lawmakers.
Vucic, born in Belgrade in 1970, had served as defense minister, first deputy prime minister and prime minister. He was elected president in 2017 and re-elected in 2022. Under the Constitution, the presidential term is five years, with a maximum of two terms for any individual.
Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic attends a press conference in Belgrade, Serbia, Sept. 27, 2026. Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. (Photo by Predrag Milosavljevic/Xinhua)

item.title: China retains top spot in gold medal tally at 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
SHANGHAI, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- China topped the gold medal tally at the 48th WorldSkills Competition as the event concluded in Shanghai on Sunday night, marking the fifth consecutive edition in which the country has taken the top spot.
Chen Jining, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee, and Chinese State Councilor Shen Yiqin attended the closing ceremony.
China's He Xiaoman received the prestigious Albert Vidal Award for her performance in the rail vehicle technology competition. The award is WorldSkills' highest honor and is presented to the competitor with the highest overall score across all skills.
China competed in all 64 skills, winning 41 gold medals, 11 silver medals, four bronze medals, and six Medals for Excellence. The Chinese delegation ranked first in the gold medal tally, the overall medal tally, and the total group points standings, marking China's best-ever performance at the WorldSkills Competition.
At the closing ceremony, the WorldSkills flag was officially passed to Japan's Aichi, which will host the 49th edition of the competition in 2028.
The WorldSkills Competition, held every two years, is widely regarded as the world's leading vocational skills competition. This year's event, held from Sept. 22 to 27, drew 1,385 participants from 68 countries and regions.
China sent 71 competitors to take part in all 64 skills at this year's competition, covering six sectors, namely transportation and logistics, construction and building technology, manufacturing and engineering technology, information and communication technology, creative arts and fashion, and social and personal services.
Seven skills made their debut at this year's competition, including rail vehicle technology, unmanned aerial systems and software testing, reflecting emerging industry trends and evolving demand for vocational skills.
Organized by WorldSkills International, the event was co-hosted by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai municipal government. The WorldSkills Conference 2026 and WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Expo were held alongside the competition.

item.title: China to work with all countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity: VP
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Chinese Vice President Han Zheng delivers a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York on Sept. 26, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- China will join hands with all other countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity and make the world a better place for all, said Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Saturday.
Han made the remarks when delivering a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
The world is witnessing intertwined changes and turbulence, protracted geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and a growing number of global challenges, he said.
Noting that Chinese President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Development Initiative at the 76th Session of the UN General Assembly, and has since then proposed the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative, Han said these initiatives provide strategic guidance for the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
He said that more and more countries want to join hands to shoulder the historic mission of addressing difficulties and challenges, and advancing the well-being of all humanity.
Han put forward four proposals:
First, safeguard the postwar international order and foster lasting peace based on common security. Turn into action the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative, and sustainable security, and reject the Cold War mindset and bloc confrontation.
Settle differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, and oppose unilateral military actions that violate the UN Charter and circumvent Security Council authorization.
Second, address the global development predicament and promote prosperity for all through openness and cooperation. Keep development at the center of the international agenda, and jointly forge a global development partnership based on unity and equality and that is balanced and inclusive.
Give priority to key areas including poverty reduction, food security and energy transition, step up resource input, and increase support for countries in the Global South. Take a people-centered approach, strive for the positive and for good, and make efforts to narrow the digital divide.
Firmly safeguard the multilateral trading system, build an open world economy, and see that economic globalization is inclusive and delivers benefits to all.
Third, advance exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations and rebuild unity and mutual trust through communication and dialogue. Use the UN platform to boost international people-to-people exchanges, promote mutual understanding and amity among all peoples and the common development of diverse civilizations.
Reject ideological prejudice, and respect the development paths and social systems decided on independently by the people of all countries. Deepen the sharing of governance practices and jointly explore ways to tackle challenges facing our times.
Fourth, stay committed to multilateralism and take steps to safeguard fairness and justice. China holds that all countries, big or small, are equal members of the international community, and that world affairs should be handled by all through consultation, and rule of law, fairness and justice in international affairs should be jointly upheld.
Countries should join forces and act together to safeguard the UN and make it stronger. China supports the UN in reforming and improving itself, and in effectively addressing global challenges including climate change and public health security.
Han pointed out that the People's Republic of China restored its lawful seat in the United Nations in 1971, which is of profound and far-reaching significance for both China and the world.
Over the past 55 years, China has been a stabilizing force in times of volatility, he said, noting that China is firmly committed to pursuing peaceful development, and has the best track record on peace and security among major countries.
A main engine driving common development, China has created two miracles at home, namely, fast economic growth and long-term social stability, and it has, over many years, contributed around 30 percent to global growth, Han said.
He said that China, a progressive force in an era of change, has always stood up for the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries, and worked toward a more just and equitable global governance system.
Han said that no matter how the international dynamics evolve, China remains unchanged in its pursuit of peace and development, in its dedication to safeguarding fairness and justice, and in its commitment to multilateralism.
During his stay in New York, Han had separate meetings with Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic, Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, and Kiribati President Taneti Maamau.
The presidents spoke highly of the major ideas and initiatives proposed by Xi, expressed admiration for China's development achievements, and reaffirmed their governments' firm adherence to the one-China principle.
They also expressed willingness to further enhance strategic mutual trust with China, deepen practical cooperation, strengthen multilateral coordination, and make greater contributions to the well-being of the people and global sustainable development.

item.title: WorldSkills Shanghai showcases new skills as AI reshapes jobs
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
The closing ceremony of the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, east China, September 27, 2026. /VCG
The 48th WorldSkills Competition concluded in Shanghai on Sunday, bringing together 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions. The event featured 64 skills, with seven making their debuts, including unmanned aerial systems, software testing and retail.
China sent 71 competitors to contest all 64 skills. Eleven competitors from east China's Jiangsu Province all received awards, winning five gold medals, two silver medals and two Medallions for Excellence across nine skills, according to Modern Express.
Over four days, competitions across 64 skills told a broader story of economic transformation: new technologies and shifting market needs are creating fresh demand, job roles are being reshaped, and the skills economies need are evolving with them.
Francis Hourant, president of WorldSkills International, said trades today are not exactly the same as they were in the 1960s, adding that the competition adjusts its portfolio to stay connected with "the reality of the industry."
New demand taking shape
The seven newcomers in Shanghai offer some of the clearest clues to where economic demand is moving.
In the unmanned aerial systems arena, competitors began with around 200 separate components. They had to assemble and calibrate a drone, write the code and prepare it for autonomous flight. Once airborne, this drone was expected to scan an unfamiliar environment, map obstacles and plan its own route – with no human intervention during the flight.
Retail presented a different scene at the Shanghai event, but still reflected the same trend. Across different modules, competitors had to take on multiple roles: arranging merchandise, pitching products to customers, hosting livestreams and handling unexpected complaints.
"Where industries develop, new occupations emerge, and WorldSkills sets up skills accordingly," said Zhang Rui, deputy director of the WorldSkills Competition China (Tianjin) Research Center.
Among the seven new skills, software testing and digital interactive media design reflect the rise of the digital economy, while unmanned aerial systems and rail vehicle technology are among the skills tied to smart manufacturing and advanced equipment, Zhang explained.
AI rewriting the job
If changing demand helps explain why new occupations are emerging, AI is reshaping what happens inside a job.
In the web technologies competition, contestants are no longer assessed simply on their ability to write code. They must analyze user needs, decide what functions a business scenario requires, complete front- and back-end development and deliver a finished product.
Wu Yingxiang, a technical expert and coach for the Chinese team in WorldSkills web technologies, said AI is making code generation much faster, thus expanding what programmers are expected to do. "Every programmer may now become a project manager and a product manager," he said.
At another hall, contestants in the digital interactive media design competition moved from product planning to image processing, video production and interaction design during more than 20 hours of competition across four days.
For Hourant, this shift points to a changing division of labor rather than an either/or choice between humans and AI. "It is not AI in the end," he said, adding that the future lies in combining human skills with AI.
Building skills for tomorrow
The skills on display in Shanghai point to a challenge: whether the supply of skilled workers can keep pace with rapidly evolving industries.
China's Ministry of Education added 27 programs to the country's vocational education catalog in July, covering fields like the digital economy, AI, the low-altitude economy and advanced equipment, with new offerings related to humanoid robots.
Shanghai Information Technology College, for example, has added four programs tailored to the city's AI industry and brought real production scenarios, technical standards and company projects into the teaching environment.
Elsewhere, schools are strengthening links with industry to keep training in step with swiftly changing industry needs. At Jiangxi Software Vocational and Technical University in east China, the campus is integrated with an industrial park, with nearly 100 companies involved in tailored training.
"Vocational education cannot be run behind closed doors," said Vice Principal of Shanghai Information Technology College Sun Pengtao. "Programs have to be updated along with industry."

item.title: Iran insists on 'negotiated solution' as Trump rejects peace proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Iranians commute past a billboard depicting former Lebanese Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and Iran's former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran on the second anniversary of Nasrallah's killing in a major strike by Israel on Beirut's southern suburbs. /Atta Kenare/AFP
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said that they seized a US submarine drone in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blockaded in the months-long Middle East war.
"Through a coordinated, complex operation involving intelligence oversight and electronic warfare, IRGC naval forces' personnel successfully captured an advanced unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) belonging to the terrorist US military," the IRGC naval forces said in a statement, according to state TV.
The top commander of Iran's army says the Hormuz Strait will remain closed until economic warfare by the United States comes to an end.
'Strait of honor'
"The Strait of Hormuz is the strait of our honor, and we will not allow the enemies of the country to use this great logistical bottleneck," Iran military official Amir Hatami told a gathering of the armed forces.
"We have said this many times that if the region is to be insecure, it is insecurity for everyone… If Iran can't do business and if Iran can't live, no one can trade and live," state media quoted him as saying.
Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that he had sent envoys around the world to pressure countries to economically isolate Iran, hailing new restrictions targeting the country's airlines and banks.
Bessent noted that Turkiye and Oman have halted incoming flights from private carrier Mahan Air, while the United Arab Emirates has stopped all flights by Iranian airlines.
Iranians walk past shops in Tehran. /atta Kenare/AFP
Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links.
Iran's ISNA news agency, citing officials, reported that five countries had revoked the Islamic republic's flight permits: Azerbaijan, Georgia, Iraq, Oman and the UAE.
'Negotiated solution' only option
Iran insisted that only diplomacy can solve its conflict with the United States and Israel after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting.
"Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi posted on social media. "Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock."
Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Trump said he rejected the plan and argued that desperation was driving the Iranians’ push for an agreement on the key waterway.
"They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Trump told reporters at the White House.
Despite Trump's public statements, mediators facilitating Iran's talks with the United States have not officially relayed a US rejection of the plan, according to Araqchi.
"We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them," Araqchi posted.
Freedom of navigation
Saudi Arabia warned UN members that attempts to block Middle East waterways are a threat to global energy security and demanded the international community do more to defend freedom of navigation.
"The international community has been absent from assuming its responsibilities in confronting all that threatens international peace and security," Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan told the United Nations General Assembly.
"The kingdom stresses the importance of guaranteeing the protection of freedom of navigation in all international waterways, foremost among them the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden," he said.
"The kingdom rejects any party's use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states, in a manner consistent with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions," he said.
Cars travel along the Hayjat al-Abd mountain road, a vital route linking Taiz with Aden and other provinces in southwestern Yemen, after overnight fighting briefly disrupted movement. /AFP
The US has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to put pressure on Tehran to stop Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, which have drastically reduced shipping through the area even as Trump repeatedly asserts that the US controls the waterway.
Renewed bombing campaign likely - Reports
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials.
It said Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections.
A US official had said earlier that discussions with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive."
The Iranians also engaged their Saudi counterparts regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping lane and taken a toll on the global economy.
Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.
"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said. If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects."
'Iran is not seeking war'
That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear program. Trump has said Tehran must never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told reporters that Iran would show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the US accepted its peace deal.
Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, the official said.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show "Face the Nation," said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues, but would not accept "bullying or coercion."
"Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons".
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on February 28.

item.title: Athletics roundup: China takes three golds as Boonson ties Asian 200m record
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Puripol Boonson of Thailand celebrates after the men's 200m final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, Sept. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Jia Yuchen)
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's Puripol Boonson tied the Asian record of 19.88 seconds in the men's 200m, while China claimed three athletics gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games on Sunday in the men's 110m hurdles, women's long jump and women's javelin.
Chen Yuanjiang started China's run of victories by winning the men's 110m hurdles in 13.15 seconds. Japan's Rachid Muratake took silver, while the Philippines' John Tolentino claimed bronze.
China had won the event at 10 consecutive Asian Games before that streak ended at the 2023 edition in Hangzhou.
"I'm thrilled. We've taken this gold medal back," said Chen, who shouted, "Who's No. 1? I am!" as he crossed the finish line.
In the women's javelin, Asian record holder Yan Ziyi needed just one throw to secure gold, launching the javelin 70.46 meters on her opening attempt. Olympic champion Haruka Kitaguchi of Japan took silver with 62.70 meters.
Yan Ziyi of China in action during the women's javelin final. (Xinhua/Luo Yuan)
Yan's mark also broke the Asian Games record of 66.09 meters set by compatriot and Olympic medalist Liu Shiying.
"I didn't expect to wrap it up in one throw. My plan was actually to take it through my first two attempts, but the first one just came out well," said Yan, who had tears in her eyes after the competition.
"I'm thrilled, and I can't wait to hear the anthem play," she said.
Asked to compare herself with Chinese shot put great Gong Lijiao, Yan played down the comparison.
"I don't think I can compare myself to her. She's a role model for me. I still have to keep learning from her and chasing what she's achieved."
Gold medalist Yan Ziyi (L) of China poses with her coach after the women's javelin. (Xinhua/Jia Yuchen)
Looking ahead to next year's world championships in Beijing and the Olympics the following year, Yan said: "I'll keep working with my coach, and I'm hoping for the top spot."
"I plan to save the new record for the world championships in Beijing, so stay tuned for that," she added.
In the women's 200m, Singapore's Shanti Pereira clocked a season-best 22.78 seconds to retain her Asian Games title, while China's 17-year-old Chen Yujie, who won the 100m in a Games record, took silver in 22.93.
Chen called Pereira "a rival worth respecting."
Chen Yujie of China celebrates after the women's 200m final. (Xinhua/Jia Yuchen)
"I planned to stay with her through the bend and then look for a chance to pass on the straight, but I'd used up too much energy in the first half," she said.
Asked about returning to high school after the Games, Chen said her parents and those around her had given her nothing but support.
"They've told me not to worry about the pressure from the internet. They never set winning gold as some hard target for me; they just want me to give it everything I've got while staying healthy."
Puripol Boonson of Thailand celebrates after the men's 200m final. (Xinhua/Lui Siu Wai)
Boonson equaled the Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye in 2019 with his 19.88-second run in the men's 200m final. China's 21-year-old Huang Youwen took silver in 20.45.
"It was the first time I'd ever raced someone at that level, and it was a great experience. I'd never felt a gap that big before," Huang said. "We were only 50 meters in, and I could already tell how fast he was. He's just really, really fast."
Looking ahead to next year's world championships, Huang added: "When you're young, you should dream big - set your sights on the result first, and figure out how to get there later."
In the women's long jump, China's Huang Yingying came from behind with a sixth-round leap of 6.55 meters to edge India's Ancy Sojan Edappilly by two centimeters for gold. Huang's compatriot Tan Mengyi took bronze with 6.46 meters.
Huang Yingying of China in action during the women's long jump final. (Xinhua/Luo Yuan)
Huang said she was far from satisfied with her performance and acknowledged that the outcome had depended on her rival's final attempts.
"Having the gold come down to whether your opponent slips up is a really nerve-wracking way to win," she said. "I need to build up my own strength, so I have more of a safety net mentally."
Huang also competed in Thursday's triple jump, taking silver.
"My main focus is still triple jump training. Doubling up in the long jump is really just for the Asian stage," she said. "I'm hoping for a better showing on a bigger stage next year at the world championships in Beijing, and at the Olympics the year after, if I can qualify."
In the men's high jump, Chinese Taipei's Fu Chao-hsuan cleared 2.25 meters to beat India's Sarvesh Kushare for gold. Qatar's 35-year-old Olympic medalist Mutaz Barshim withdrew from the final.
Earlier Sunday, Japan's Hayato Katsuki clocked 3:03:36 to beat China's Zhou Yingcheng for the men's marathon race walk title, while Kazakhstan's Yasmina Toxanbayeva won the women's race in 3:22:20. China's Danzengquzong and Ma Li took silver and bronze, respectively, in the women's event.
The first round of the 4x100m relays was also held Sunday, with China's men's and women's teams both winning their heats to advance to the finals.

item.title: Xi's letter to dialogue marking GDI's 5th anniversary draws global acclaim
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
"Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind," Chinese President Xi Jinping said in a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI), held Friday at the UN headquarters in New York, United States.
The letter resonated widely with participants and observers worldwide, who said it demonstrates Xi's firm support for the global development cause. Five years on, they noted, the GDI has taken root and borne fruit, pooling strong synergy for common development.
In the letter, Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted.
African scholars visit a smart blueberry cultivation facility in Jinhua, east China's Zhejiang Province, May 23, 2026. /VCG
'A cornerstone of transformative progress'
"The GDI has become a cornerstone of transformative progress and an outstanding example in the field of global governance," said Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended the dialogue and heard the letter read out.
Five years ago, he said, the landmark initiative came into being, offering a compelling framework for responding to global crises and for cooperation among countries. Xi's initiative, focused on people's well-being and sustainable development, has won broad recognition across the world.
"From President Xi's letter, we read a kind of leadership – the world needs this kind of leadership, one that upholds mutual respect and looks to global development," said E.P. Chet Greene, Antigua and Barbuda's minister of foreign affairs, trade and Barbuda affairs.
The GDI genuinely puts people at the center, Greene said, adding that without the initiative, the world today – the Global South in particular – would not be seeing the progress it has achieved.
'Not just a principle, but a practical tool for progress'
An important lesson from the GDI is that "development is not just a principle, but a practical tool for progress," said Abdoulkader Houssein Omar, Djibouti's minister of foreign affairs and international cooperation, who also attended the dialogue.
The expansion of the Group of Friends of the GDI, he added, demonstrates broad support for a development agenda rooted in solidarity, partnership and pragmatic action.
"More important than infrastructure is empowerment," said Robert Lawrence Kuhn, chairman of The Kuhn Foundation. In his view, the GDI has genuinely helped Global South countries build up their development capacity.
Under the GDI framework, Kuhn noted, many developing countries have drawn on China's development experience and gradually formed industrial systems suited to their own national conditions.
Chinese and foreign engineers exchange views at the 600-MW Monsoon Wind Power Project in southern Laos, December 28, 2025. /VCG
'Pooling strength for common development'
As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said in the letter.
The call drew warm responses. Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the GDI has pushed the international community to place development at the core of the agenda, truly responding to the pressing needs of developing countries.
The changes the GDI has brought to Africa and the Global South are embodied in the reality Xi described, said Stephen Ndegwa, executive director of South-South Dialogues, a Nairobi-based think tank. From drinking water and electricity to technology empowerment and digital connectivity, he said, these concrete actions put into practice the vision of "common development and win-win cooperation."
The development of the Global South is crucial to the world's future, and China's leadership in driving it is invaluable, said Lawrence Freeman, a US economist and Africa affairs analyst. China has demonstrated to the world that the sustainable development goals can be achieved, he said, and will help pool an even greater force for global sustainable development.

item.title: Xi's state visit leads to new progress in constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the United States has led to new progress in a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said after Xi wrapped up his U.S. visit on Friday.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi's state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25.
President Xi and President Donald Trump had a candid and in-depth exchange of views in a friendly atmosphere of mutual respect on strategic and overarching issues concerning China-U.S. relations and the broader global landscape, Wang said.
Since President Trump began his second term, the two heads of state have maintained close exchanges, including three in-person meetings and five phone talks, and fostered a pattern of interaction marked by mutual respect and sincerity, said Wang, noting this has become the most valuable strategic asset in China-U.S. relations.
An important political outcome of the visit is that President Xi and President Trump further enriched the substance of the new positioning of China-U.S. relations and have agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang said.
Respect means respecting each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respecting each country's choice of social system and development path, and respecting the other side's core interests and major concerns, Wang said.
Fairness, Wang continued, means pursuing mutually beneficial cooperation and handling differences through consultation, rejecting a zero-sum game in which one side's gain comes at the expense of the other's, and not seeking unilateral absolute advantage.
Reciprocity means that the two countries are equal in sovereignty, that neither side stands above the other, that neither engages in hegemonic nor bullying behavior, that each side's concerns are addressed on an equal basis, and that cooperation across various fields develops in a balanced manner, Wang said.
Noting that President Xi has pointed out that a stable China-U.S. economic and trade relationship requires both expanding the list of cooperation and shortening the list of problems, Wang said that the U.S. side should treat Chinese companies fairly, resolve problems through dialogue and negotiations, and promote the sustained, stable and positive development of China-U.S. economic and trade relations.
The fentanyl abuse problem in the United States is not caused by China, but China has always acted with the utmost goodwill and made every effort to assist the U.S. side in addressing the fentanyl crisis, Wang noted, adding that the two heads of state tasked the law enforcement agencies of the two countries with continuing to strengthen cooperation and jointly combat transnational crime.
To promote people-to-people exchanges between China and the United States, President Xi has announced a series of new measures, including inviting 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchange and study programs over the next five years, Wang said.
One piece of good news that has been particularly welcomed by the American public is that two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will soon arrive at Zoo Atlanta, Wang added.
During the visit, Wang said, the two heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on major international and regional issues of common concern and agreed to strengthen coordination to make due contributions to world peace and development.
President Xi also encouraged relevant parties to stay committed to peace, supported the United States and Iran in returning to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, resuming dialogue and negotiations at an early date, and ultimately reaching a comprehensive agreement covering the nuclear issue, Wang said.
During the visit, President Xi and President Trump also had an in-depth exchange of views on artificial intelligence (AI), pointing out that the two countries should leverage respective strengths rather than guard against each other, Wang said.
The two heads of state agreed to make good use of AI dialogue mechanisms between the two countries and jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI, Wang added.
Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Wang said that China and the United States are both permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, and it is their shared responsibility to uphold the postwar international order and prevent the resurgence of militarism.
China and the United States will respectively host the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Leaders' Summit in the fourth quarter of this year, Wang said, adding that the two heads of state confirmed their mutual support, which will continue to inject momentum into cooperation in the Asia-Pacific and global governance.

item.title: Mid-Autumn Festival: Better Than Heaven
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
What will Chang'e discover when she leaves the Moon Palace to visit Earth this Mid-Autumn Festival?
As enchanting as heaven is, nothing touches the heart like the bustling warmth of the mortal world.
Under the same full moon, love and longing cross mountains, seas, and all borders. It turns out the greatest beauty was never the cold heights of the cosmos, but the warm glow of reunited homes.
Together under the gentle moonlight, let us celebrate.
Beneath every full moon, may you find the joy of long-awaited reunions, and the blessing of peace year after year.
Happy Mid-Autumn Festival!

item.title: Mid-Autumn Festival: Voices of global 'Chinese Bridge' youngsters
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Ahead of the 2026 Mid-Autumn Festival, the candidates of the 19th "Chinese Bridge"—Chinese Proficiency Competition for Foreign Secondary School Students traveled to Beijing and Tianjin. Through contests and cultural study tours, they explored China and experienced the enduring charm of Mid-Autumn. Known as the global "Olympics" of Chinese learning, "Chinese Bridge" brings us voices from Mandarin enthusiasts across five continents, sharing what the festival means to them.
